meta_title: When check-ins aren't getting through — Anbu
meta_desc: What to check when a check-in arrives late, or steps and location don't come with it.
page_lead: Sometimes a check-in arrives late, or steps and location don't come with it. In most cases, turning on one permission on the sender's phone fixes it.
mockup_caption: All three notices are shown together here for explanation. In reality they appear one at a time, only when they apply, and disappear once resolved.
mockup_hint: See where this is on screen

dialog.lead: Tapping the yellow notice opens this window right away.
dialog.title: @stability_battery_dialog_title

items.q: I keep getting a “💗 Wellness check needed” notification on my phone. It seems the check-in is only sent when I open the app.
items.q2: My family got a “@notifications_level_caution” alert saying “@noti_caution_missing_body”
a: To save battery, Android slows down or stops apps you don't use often. Anbu wakes up briefly once a day at the set time to send your check-in, so if this restriction applies, it misses that moment and nothing is sent until you use your phone again.
If no check-in arrives within two hours past the set time, your family receives the alert above. This can happen even when the sender is perfectly fine and only the delivery was delayed.

On the sender's phone, open the app and look near the top for a yellow notice saying “@stability_battery_warning_short”. Tapping it goes straight to the settings screen, and once you lift the restriction the notice disappears.

items.q: Why is this the only notice in yellow?
a: It means check-ins are not stopped altogether — they may just be delayed. Notices shown in red mean a feature is actually blocked.

dialog.lead:
Tapping the red notice brings up Android's own permission request. Allowing it there is all you need.
However, if you have already declined several times, Android stops showing that request. The window below appears instead.
dialog.title: @gs_activity_permission_settings_title

items.q: My family member's step count isn't showing. The “You walked N steps today” notification never arrives.
a: Along with the check-in signal, Anbu sends that day's step count so family can see how much they moved. If the step permission is off on the sender's phone, the check-in still goes through, but the step count is left out.
On that phone, open the app and look below the safety code for a red notice saying “@gs_activity_permission_denied_warning”. Tapping it asks for the permission again.

items.q: Do you look at anything besides steps?
a: Only the step count is sent. We do not check where you have been or which apps you have used.

sections.heading: An emergency request came without a location

dialog.lead:
Tapping the red notice brings up Android's own permission request. Allowing it there is all you need.
However, if you have already declined several times, Android stops showing that request. The window below appears instead.
dialog.title: @location_permission_settings_title

items.q: I received an emergency request, but there is no [@notifications_view_location] button on the alert.
a: Location permission is required to send the current location along when the emergency button is pressed. Without it, the emergency alert still reaches everyone in the family, but where they are does not go with it.
On the sender's phone, open the app and look below the [@subject_home_emergency_button] button for a red notice. Tapping it asks for the permission again.

items.q: Are you tracking my location all the time?
a: No. We collect no location at all under normal circumstances. Only when [@subject_home_emergency_button] is pressed do we take a single reading at that moment and pass it to family, and that information is erased after a day.

items.q: I tapped the notice, but the settings screen didn't open properly.
a: The name and location of the settings screen differ slightly by manufacturer. Please open your Settings app, find Anbu, and check the permissions section directly.

items.q: After I arrived abroad, my family got a “@notifications_level_caution” alert.
a: Anbu sends check-ins by the local time shown on your phone. But for the first day or two after you arrive in another country, the new time hasn't been passed on yet, so the check-in is still expected on the time of the country you left. Because of the time difference, it looks as if the check-in hasn't arrived, so your family may get an alert, and your own phone may show a check-in reminder in the middle of the night.
You are fine — only the time is off. Once the first check-in goes out on local time, everything returns to normal on its own.
After you arrive, please open the Anbu app once. The moment you open it, the new time is passed on, and from then on check-ins follow local time. Please open it once again when you come back, too.

If you have set Do Not Disturb hours, please also open the app once when you arrive. That way the hours you chose not to get alerts (for example, 10 PM to 7 AM) move to local time. If you don't, the time of the country you left stays in effect, so alerts may ring in the middle of the night or stay silent during the day.

items.q: Do I need to change the check-in time while traveling?
a: No. The time you set applies to wherever you are now. If you set 6 PM, the check-in goes out at 6 PM local time while you travel, too.
